profile.campus_mw_context: The 128,715-sq. ft. data center in Sterling, VA, offers 11 MW of IT capacity and features robust connectivity options with high bandwidth and high-availability circuits and a number of metro and long-haul networks.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA4 is a small facility by AI standards: 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet, roughly 275 racks at 40 kW per rack.

The scale places it outside Virginia's top tier. Of 330 mapped data centers in the state, only 25 publish capacity figures, and this campus ranks 26th among them. It accounts for under 1% of the 1,603 MW Virginia discloses. The published figure is IT load, not total campus power, so the gap between what it draws and what it delivers to servers is not visible here.

Its emphasis is connectivity, with multiple metro and long-haul circuits. That suits distributed inference and enterprise workloads more than frontier training, where absolute power density dominates. Network quality does not substitute for megawatts.

What the data cannot show is whether this facility sits near larger unpublished capacity. Virginia has 305 mapped or unpublished facilities whose load is unknown, and the state's true aggregate could be materially larger than the 1,603 MW disclosed. This entry describes one building, not the constraint it operates under.
